claim: An automatic compiler can generate correct and competitive modular residue sieves for structured families k*b^n+c.
An adaptive sieve bound can improve end-to-end time or energy on at least some regimes.
Automatic engine routing can remain within 3 percent of the best measured static engine on held-out workloads.
An asynchronous CPU/GPU pipeline can reduce idle time and total processing time on target workloads.
Generic fixed-size CUDA modular arithmetic can beat CPU GMP/FLINT end-to-end on sufficiently large uniform batches.
Proof integration from the start can reduce recalculation and validation risk at acceptable total cost.
A portfolio scheduler using frequent intermediate signals can improve a selected objective over fixed allocation.
The combination of a family language, congruence compilation, routing, and certification can constitute a distinct contribution.
